questions.q: What incident from the Intermediate-tier project escalated into a board-level security review at Hartwell Regional Utilities?
options: A phishing email that reached the CEO's inbox
An overly broad firewall rule that went undetected until a 3 a.m. alert forced the question of what else looked like it
A failed software update that took down the billing system
A lost company laptop reported by an employee
questions.explain: The board's reasoning was blunt: if one overly permissive firewall rule sat undetected that long, the board wanted to know what else might be hiding in more consequential parts of the network, especially OT/SCADA.

questions.q: Who is Hartwell's CISO, and what is his role in this capstone?
options: Howard Okonjo — the executive sponsor whose name is attached to the program's budget and who presents progress to the board
Mara Voss — the CISO who personally wrote the firewall rule
Howard Okonjo — an outside auditor with no ongoing involvement
The IT Director, who happens to share Howard Okonjo's name
questions.explain: Howard Okonjo is Hartwell's CISO and the named executive sponsor of the board-mandated program; his credibility is tied to whether the program delivers in 90 days.

questions.q: What were the four specific workstreams the board mandated and funded?
options: A new antivirus rollout, a password policy update, an employee handbook revision, and a help-desk ticketing tool
A zero-trust network segmentation pilot, a consolidated Azure/AWS identity view, Python-based security automation, and a formal GRC risk register
A full enterprise-wide zero-trust rollout, a new SIEM purchase, a security awareness campaign, and a new firewall vendor
A compliance audit, a penetration test, a disaster-recovery drill, and a vendor risk assessment
questions.explain: The board funded a scoped zero-trust segmentation pilot, one consolidated dual-cloud identity view, Python-based automation to replace manual access reviews, and a formal, owned GRC risk register.

questions.q: What is Mara Voss's new role at the start of this capstone, and what changed?
options: She remains a SOC analyst, just with a bigger ticket queue
She was promoted to Security Engineer — now designing and building controls, not just operating and triaging them
She moved to a sales engineering role
She became the new CISO, replacing Howard Okonjo
questions.explain: The Intermediate project's incident response led to Mara's promotion to Security Engineer, shifting her focus from detection-and-response operations to designing and building the controls themselves.

questions.q: What budget and timeline did the board approve for Phase 1 of this program?
options: $340,000 and 90 days to deliver a working pilot and report back to the board
No budget was approved, only a verbal commitment to revisit later
$3.4 million and a five-year roadmap
$340,000 with no deadline attached
questions.explain: The board approved a $340,000 Phase 1 budget and gave the program 90 days to deliver a working pilot and present results — the reason Lesson 20 of this capstone is a board presentation.
